issues.failure_explanation: Defining e^{tK_i} on C_b(Omega) requires the frozen one-dimensional flows to exist for all t and remain in Omega so that g in C_b(Omega) can be evaluated; this is not implied by the stated hypotheses (unique, global solutions of the full system in closed Omega). Counterexample within the hypotheses: Omega = closed unit disk, F(x,y) = (-y,x): the full flow is rotation (unique, global, jointly continuous, Omega-invariant), but the frozen flow x' = F_1(x,x_2) = -x_2 gives x(t) = x_1 - x_2 t, which exits Omega, so g(sigma(t,x_1),x_2) is undefined. The sub-semigroups, the splitting operators V_1, V_2 and the algorithms of remApp/rem324 are therefore not well-defined as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that Omega is invariant under all frozen coordinate flows (or take Omega = R^N) and that the frozen 1-D problems have unique global solutions.
issues.overall_effect: The splitting construction is ill-defined for general closed Omega; only special domains (e.g., R^N, or the paper's examples) are safe.
issues.title: Frozen sub-semigroups on C_b(Omega) not well-defined (missing invariance hypothesis)

issues.failure_explanation: The order-3 and higher routines (remApp (c), app33) evaluate the frozen solution maps at complex sub-step durations (t*abar/2n, t*a/n, ...) and at complex intermediate states. For general nonlinear F — the paper's standing scope is uniquely solvable IVPs, with no analyticity assumed — the frozen flow built by separation of variables is a real-time object; complex-time evaluation requires holomorphic extension of F and complex-time existence, neither assumed nor discussed (e.g., F_1(x) = 1+|x| has no holomorphic extension; u' = u^2 has poles in complex time). The routines are well-defined only for holomorphic frozen equations with entire flows (the paper's linear examples), so the advertised general implementability of the high-order schemes is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the advertised scope of the high-order routines to holomorphic F whose frozen flows extend to the required complex times, and state that intermediate values are complex (output realness relies on the conjugate-palindromic coefficient structure).
issues.overall_effect: The general input-output contract of the order->=3 routines fails; their scope must be restricted to systems whose frozen flows extend holomorphically to the needed complex times.
issues.title: High-order routines require complex-time evaluation of real frozen flows
issues.why_classification: The repair is a genuine scope restriction on the advertised generality, though the paper's concrete examples remain covered.
